summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with subsequent gastrostomy tube management and later bypass reversal) was admitted for nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhea, and abdominal pain localized to the G-tube site after restarting tube feeds and then developing poor oral tolerance. She was managed supportively with bowel rest, intravenous fluids, antiemetics, resumption of ulcer/GERD prophylaxis (pantoprazole and sucralfate), and close monitoring of intake/output and labs, without evidence of fever, bleeding, or other signs of infection during hospitalization. Pain control was transitioned from IV morphine to oral oxycodone once she tolerated diet; Psychiatry was consulted for anxiety, and a clonidine patch was considered but not continued due to intermittently low systolic blood pressures. By hospital day 2 her diet was advanced to regular and was well tolerated, symptoms improved, and she was discharged home ambulatory and hemodynamically stable with return precautions and continuation of home medications including PRN ondansetron and short-course oxycodone.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection
